Quality log

Every problem found tonight is fixed where it starts and gets a check, so it can't come back. 1. Stand-up shorts started with no mic and the house lights up (an open task in slop-tv-content's handoff notes). make_short.py now starts a stand-up short with Brad on his mark, mic in hand, and every light at the level it had reached at the cut. Checked by eye on episode_010_short_1. 2. Shorts ended with about 11 s of dead picture: closing applause plus a shrug clip running to its end. New engine flag end_applause (off for shorts that end on a punchline, so they get a laugh instead of applause), and those shorts end on the line plus a 3.2 s tail. New QC rule: a short with more than 5 s of tail FAILs. 3. Recompiling Unity during Play mode broke the eye-gaze controller (IndexOutOfRange every frame, render stuck). Fixed in GazeController. The worker now waits until Unity says it's ready before every render. 4. Clearance false alarms held 4 of 7 Brad scripts: "Only Brad" and "Let Dana" at the start of a sentence read as unknown full names; "Exit Strategy" (our own episode 4 title) flagged; "the last he" matched the real title 'The Last Leg' at 86%. All fixed in slopwriter's checks, with regression tests; near-miss puns like "saturday nite live" are still caught. 5. The ledger lock only worked inside one process, so the batch writer, the worker and the web app could fork the hash chain. It's now a file lock across processes. 6. Natural movement is now measured on every render (qc_report.py section 4b): one clip used for more than 40 % of a character's gestures, the same clip three times running, a speaker with no gesture or expression through a line longer than 6 s, and the share of lines a listener reacts to (warn below 80 %). The numbers go to Renders/qc_history.jsonl so each episode can be compared with the last. Baseline: stand-up episode 10 has listeners reacting to 100 % of lines; podcast episode 8 only 56 %, guest frozen on all 8 long answers, 8 of 9 guest gestures the same nod. 7. Cause of the frozen podcast guests: slopwriter's exporter only gave the host talking gestures. New podcast episodes give the guest varied talking loops (never the same twice running), and the listener nods, leans in, takes notes or smiles during the other person's longer lines. 8. Repeat hand-offs took a new episode number and left a duplicate script file. They now reuse the project's own number and file. 9. Brad's YouTube titles now carry season and episode, one season per club set: S1 = club 1 (eps 1-5), S2 = club 2 (eps 6-8), S3 = club 3 (ep 9 on; tonight's sets are S3 E3 onwards). youtube_meta.py also handles several shorts per episode. 10. Provenance: tonight's 6 hand-offs (ledger 358-393) and one leftover-files capture (380) were recorded as you. They were me. Correction event 397 names them; hand-off now takes an actor, and restarts no longer capture leftovers as your edits. 11. Clipping: episode 13's mix peaked at +2.3 dBFS where the goodnight, two applause sounds and the outro music overlap, and +0.6 dBFS at the intro. The renders had no master limiter. Added one to the final mix (peaks at -2 dBFS, no auto-gain, loudness unchanged at -18.4 LUFS on the test). 12. A T-posed body stood on the performer mark through all of episode 13. My first guess (the offstage MC) was wrong; the re-render still showed it. Probing the open scene found the real cause: a Sidekick "Combined Character" saved at the scene root of standup_club_03 (not in git, so added since the last commit), with no animator, standing at the origin. Removed and the scene saved. The build now removes any humanoid outside the cast that has no animator controller, on every set, and warns; offstage cast members also can't carry a body. QC can't see a T-pose, so this guard is what protects every episode from now on. 13. Made-up products and places in podcast adverts ("Sandwich Taxi", "Puddle Insurance", "Gate Two") held the Rex Pivot script as possible real people. Names made only of ordinary dictionary words are now a low (non-blocking) note; real brands are still the denylist's and the reviewers' job. 14. The tail check measured from the last line, so every stand-up "failed" on Brad's designed walk-off. It now measures from the last line or move: episode 13's outro is 8.4 s, a pass. 15. More clearance false alarms, "Add Clementine" and "Let Grayson": any ordinary word that starts a sentence is no longer read as part of a name ("Then Marcus Brody" is now reported as "Marcus Brody"). 16. The drafter itself declares invented names in a production note ("Fictional names: Add Clementine, the former herd cow"), and the name check flagged that very note. Names a draft declares under "Fictional names:" now count as ours, and the sentence-start rule handles markdown bold after a colon. 17. The YouTube upload copy (-14 LUFS) came out at -0.1 dBTP: linear loudness normalisation adds 4-5 dB and the peaks go with it. youtube_master.py now limits after normalising and refuses a copy over -1 dBTP. Episode 13's copy: -14.3 LUFS, -1.6 dBTP. 18. Better jokes (your ask). The table reader gave Brad: Undo 5/5 on nearly everything, so it gave the writers nothing to aim at. New joke doctor: a different model from the drafter scores every spoken line out of 10 against a professional bar (5 = a smile, 7 = a real laugh, 9 = the one people quote), says why each weak line misses (punch word not last, setup too long, explains itself, concept not joke) and writes two sharper versions; the reviser rewrites from that; up to 3 rounds until the script averages 7.5 with no line under 6. Every round is saved (05-jokes-vN.md) and its scores go in the project chat, so you can see each script improve. On from round two's Brad sets and podcasts. 19. Process fix (my mistake): the Sloane Vantage episode was held by a model reviewer's HIGH finding that the "question in the milk churn" copies the real podcast's signature segment. My rescue step re-ran clearance, a second reviewer passed it, and I approved it. The ritual itself is your decision (D-046 in slop-tv-content: the milk churn replaced the original's ritual), so the episode is within your rules, but re-rolling a reviewer until it says yes is wrong. From now on rescues only clear rule-based false alarms; anything a model reviewer blocks waits for you. Please look at Sloane (podcast episode_012) with that in mind. 20. Render failures now get one automatic retry (the first podcast build after the stand-up renders timed out loading the set). The worker re-reads its state every pass, so stuck items can be requeued without a restart. 21. On the news show, names in the linked stories (Hubble Space Telescope, a company, a place) count as known: they're the news. Real people in them still get the S-004 "keep it attributed" note. 22. YouTube upload files are ready for the rendered Brad sets (S3 E3, E5 to E9): -14 LUFS upload copy, a thumbnail from a picked close-up with a hook (e.g. "THEY PICKED / THE BLINK"), title, hook and summary in Publishing/youtube_metadata.json (each marked "not yet reviewed by the owner"), and youtube.txt per folder. Episode numbers in a season are set explicitly, so S3 E2 stays reserved for episode 10 (still waiting for your review). 23. Podcast dead air: QC failed every podcast render (including the already-released episode 8) for digital silence between lines. The room-tone bed was a generated clip near -66 LUFS played at 0.18, so it vanished. Normalised it to -40 LUFS (measured -45 after generation) at 0.8, the fix the news set already had. Rex re-renders with it; the shorts get it too. 24. The worker now renders two shorts after every episode so the shorts don't starve while new episodes keep arriving. Podcast builds that outlast the MCP bridge's timeout are waited out and retried; Rex's episode built on the retry. 25. The joke doctor could hand off a worse script: one rewrite took Daylight Saving from 6.0 to 5.5, and the last rewrite was never scored at all. Now every rewrite is scored, and if an earlier version scored higher it's restored as the final draft (recorded as such). 26. The writers put Sloane in Brad's audience heckling him, and the hand-off refused because she wasn't one of the template's seated audience. A crossover like that is good writing: the exporter now seats any speaking audience member at a free seat. 27. Restarting a batch skipped whatever it was in the middle of (Merch, Doctor Vera Doze). Ideas now only count as tried once they finish, and a project that was already written and cleared goes straight to approval instead of being written again. 28. Measured result of the podcast movement work: Rex Pivot Returns (the first podcast with guest gestures) has listeners reacting to 88 % of lines (36 of 41) and no frozen speaker, against 56 % and 8 frozen lines on the released episode 8. Shows with an outro (music over the logo) now get 6 s more tail in QC; Rex's ending is 12.3 s. 29. A batch lost the start of "Brad: Subscribers" to a git lock held by another process (the web app's status check runs git outside the ledger lock). Git calls in the ledger now wait and retry when the index is locked. The ledger stayed intact (verified); Subscribers goes into the next round. 30. News shorts failed validation: the ticker and name straps pointed at lines the short had cut. Shorts now drop the broadcast graphics (shorts carry no text overlays, D-037; the news-graphics exception D-052 is for the show itself), and every short opens on the shot the episode was on at the cut, so the first camera cue is at 0 as the checker requires. check_show.py knows the new end_applause key. 31. "Stool's Turndown Service" held Night Shift: "turndown" isn't in the word list. A word that splits into two ordinary words now counts as ordinary. Trade-off: a real surname built the same way (Woodward) gets a low note rather than a block; the two model reviewers still check every script for real people. 32. Ollie's lip sync: her crossover podcast gave her voice 19 calibrated lines, so episode 12 (The Comments), which failed twice on her 3-frame lag, is back in the render queue. 33. Repeat across parallel batches: Penny's and Barnaby's podcast episodes (podcast episodes 14 and 19) open on nearly the same joke ("born, according to one source; my mother declined to comment") with near-identical titles. Two batches wrote them in parallel and neither could see the other. Writers, the table read and the joke doctor now see every approved-but-unreleased script of the show too, not just released ones. For you: release one of the two, or have one rewritten. 34. Hands in faces (my mistake): looking at the podcast thumbnail candidates, every guest's raised hand was going into their face. The cause was the pointing-finger talking loop (talk_point) I put in the guests' gesture rotation (item 7); on a seated guest it drives the hand into the face. Removed from the rotation; the 7 podcast episodes rendered with it (Rex, Tessa, Penny, Vera, Ollie, Dana, Barnaby) are being re-rendered, and their shorts (which don't use it) stay. The wrist trace is only recorded for prop holders, so QC can't catch this yet (see open items). 35. QC's contact sheets were silently missing all night: the worker runs inside the project's Python environment, where `python3` has no Pillow, so qc_report.py skipped the sheets (and left raw frames behind). The worker now calls the system Python for the tools, and every render from tonight is being re-checked so the sheets exist for your review. 36. Podcast shorts got the stand-up's 3.2 s of laugh room after the punchline, dead air without a crowd, and one failed the 5 s tail rule. The laugh room is now for stand-up only. 37. The writers invented "Nell" to heckle Brad; production has no body or voice for her, so the hand-off could only write a requirements note. Autopilot now checks every speaker against production's characters before clearance and has the reviser give unknown speakers' lines to an existing regular (or cut them). Recommended For You was recast, re-cleared, re-approved and handed off as episode 30. 38. YouTube files ready for Brad S3 E10 to E20 (episodes 18 to 28): titles, hooks from each set's biggest laugh, summaries, thumbnails ("DISHWASHER SAFE", "YOUR FRIDGE READS LIPS"...). The jokes in these later rounds are visibly sharper than round one's, which is the joke doctor's effect. Thumbnails all use the same close-up angle; a varied pick (a wide with the crowd, a gesture) would help the channel page. 39. "six minute" matched the real title 'Sixty Minutes' at 86% and held Sloane Takes a Day Off. A number in a title now has to match exactly ("sixty minutes" is still caught), with a regression test. 40. Model reviewers kept flagging what you'd already settled in D-046 (the show's name, the milk churn): they weren't told. New prompts/show_rules/conversations_dairy_farmer.md states the decision for every writer and reviewer of the podcast; they still flag anything else that points at a real show. Rex Pivots to Comedy was held on the show-name point alone before this landed; it's left for you rather than re-cleared. 41. Shorts counted the last line's pause twice (once before the logo cut, again in the tail), so podcast shorts with a long final pause ran 5.6 s past the line and failed QC. The tail is now just the hold after the logo cut; the failed shorts are re-rendering. 42. Brad: Coffee failed the render's foot-slide check: the script sat Brad down just before his last line, and the exporter's automatic "stand up before goodnight" landed on the same moment, so he walked to the stool and straight back with his feet sliding. If no line is spoken while seated, the exporter now leaves him standing. Open (not fixed tonight): - Lip sync for voices with fewer than 4 lines on record uses a typical offset (Ollie's long line in episode 12 came out 3 frames late). Worked around tonight by giving her a podcast; the real fix (a new voice calibrates on its own lines in that render) needs an engine change and tests. - A hand-in-face QC check: the render should trace both hands against the head for every speaker (today wrist_trace.json is only written for prop holders), and QC should fail a hand inside the head bounds. Engine work with tests. - Two shorts from Brad episode 11 failed lip sync by 2 frames early (the full episode passed). Probably the cut point changes the voice's timing fit; to look at with the lip-sync work above. Next on the list: - Stand-up: vary Brad's gestures (ep 10 Ollie laughs 3 times in a row with the same clip). - Lift the movement checks from WARN to FAIL once new episodes pass them, so the bar only goes up.

The night so far
